newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday January 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday January 8.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* State games committee declared a winning two billion lire lottery ticket invalid because of a technical problem. Finance minister Vincenzo Visco decided to open an inquiry (all).
* Prime Minister Romano Prodi, attending a celebration for 200 years of the Italian flag, said the government would never tolerate secession (all).
* In an interview, Italian Renewal party leader and Foreign minister Lamberto Dini says he favours a "broader political majority" to carry out political reforms and to join EMU (Corriere della Sera).

* The Constitutional Court today begins to assess the validity of 30 proposed referendums, ranging from abolishing the residual element of proportional representation to decriminalising the use of marijuana (all).
* Opposition parties are split over prospects for a bi-cameral commission for constitutional reforms (all).

* Engineering employers association formally rejected a government proposal for a new wage deal but said it was ready to resume talks with metalworkers' unions. Trades unions said they were calling 10 hours of strikes and were ready to stage a general strike (all).

* The economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter of 1996 with gross domestic product rising 0.7 percent year-on-year. Deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni said the increase in GDP "confirms that the economy is on the road to recovery" (all).

* Information technology group Olivetti shares jumped to close 7.35 percent higher on confirmed reports that Gianmario Rossignolo, chairman of white goods group Zanussi, is working with U.S. financier Edward Gottesman of the Centenary group in a bid to acquire Olivetti's ailing PC division. Talks are said to have reached "an important point". Another bid of 100 billion lire cash, reportedly put forward by U.S. corporate debt trader Gary Klesch, is said to have been rejected by Olivetti at the end of December (Sole 24 Ore).
* Prodi said inflation data for January will not be good on statistical grounds but the figures will improve in February.
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
